title: Brave Search API x402 for Autonomous AI Agent Payments
summary: Brave Search API x402 facilitates automated micro-transactions for data retrieval. Developers can configure agent workflows to handle status codes.
body_markdown:
## Implement x402 for instant agent payments


When a token expires on the Saturday of a long weekend, nothing alerts anyone until the Monday invoice run. Brave Search API’s x402 update solves this by enabling your AI agents to pay for individual data requests instantly using USDC on the Base blockchain.


This transition from monthly billing to per-query settlement allows your autonomous systems to manage their own operational expenses without human intervention in the payment loop.


### Brave launches x402 payment protocol


On November 13, 2024,[Brave](https://brave.com/blog/search-api-agentic-payments/) launched the x402 protocol. This provides a machine-native alternative to traditional API key management.


The moment a connector is configured in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , an agent can call it immediately. Registering an integration once allows it to function as both a flow step and a tool schema on a per-project MCP server, accessible by Claude, ChatGPT, or custom agents.


There is no secondary catalog to maintain or export; the same integration action found in the` packages/pieces` open-source repo runs in a flow or as an MCP tool. A catalog that requires re-integration for agents is just a second migration.


- This broad data set helps your agents avoid the knowledge gaps found in smaller, niche crawlers.
- Your agent retrieves fresh signals rather than cached data that has decayed for a week.
-


> A catalog that requires re-integration for agents is just a second migration.


High-fidelity results justify the immediate cost. This volume of fresh data ensures that when your agent triggers a payment, it receives the quality it paid for.


### How the x402 protocol functions


By utilizing **HTTP 402 Payment Required** headers, the x402 protocol challenges a requesting agent for a micropayment before the server returns the search results.


When a model identifies a need for external data, it receives a Lightning Network invoice in the response header. Your agent pays it via a connected wallet and resubmits the request with proof of payment.


### Managing the agentic wallet


For an agent to settle these invoices autonomously, it must have programmatic access to a Lightning-enabled wallet. This wallet typically exists as a separate service or a node connection, such as an Alby account or a dedicated LND node.


The agent uses a specific SDK to communicate with this wallet. When the 402 header arrives, the library extracts the invoice, requests a signature from the wallet service, and returns the cryptographic proof to the agent for the final API call.


This protocol eliminates "sandbox rot" where developers test against stale data because they lack the budget for a full production tier. Every environment now operates on the same pay-per-call logic.


By shifting the financial burden to your agent's wallet, you can audit exact per-task costs, eliminating the waste of paying for idle capacity.
